story_title: Global Natural Disasters and Mortality Trends: A Century of Data
story_subtitle: Analyzing the deadliest natural disasters across entities, years, and types to uncover historical patterns and critical insights

story_pieces.narration: Droughts caused the highest single-year death toll in 1928 with 3,000,000 fatalities, far exceeding other disaster types in that year.
story_pieces.question: When was the deadliest year for drought-related deaths, and how does it compare to other disaster types?
story_pieces.visualization: line chart (years vs. drought deaths with overlay of other disaster types)

story_pieces.narration: The 1976 earthquake in Tangshan, China, caused 276,994 deaths, marking the single most lethal earthquake in recorded history.
story_pieces.question: Which earthquake caused the highest number of deaths, and what was its impact?
story_pieces.visualization: bar chart (earthquake years vs. deaths with highlight of 1976)

story_pieces.narration: Epidemics accounted for over 25 million deaths between 1900 and 2017, outpacing all other disaster categories combined.
story_pieces.question: How do epidemic-related deaths compare to other disaster types over the past century?
story_pieces.visualization: stacked bar chart (decades vs. deaths by disaster type)

story_pieces.narration: Extreme weather events saw a sharp increase in deaths from 2010 onwards, with 57,188 fatalities recorded in 2010 alone.
story_pieces.question: Has the mortality rate from extreme weather events been increasing over time?
story_pieces.visualization: area chart (years vs. extreme weather deaths with trendline)

story_pieces.narration: Floods were the deadliest disaster type overall, responsible for 11.6 million deaths between 1900 and 2017, followed by droughts and earthquakes.
story_pieces.question: Which disaster type caused the most deaths historically, and how do the types compare?
story_pieces.visualization: ranked bar chart (disaster types vs. total deaths)
